Fit linear models to spectral peaks extracted from the wavelet spectra to astronomical cycles multiplied by sedimentation rate x

Source: R/flmw.R
flmw.Rd

The flmw function is used calculate the linear correlation for a list of astronomical cycles transformed using a range of sedimentation rates and then compared to spectral peaks of a wavelet spectra

Usage

flmw(
  wavelet = NULL,
  sedrate_low = NULL,
  sedrate_high = NULL,
  spacing = NULL,
  cycles = c(NULL),
  x_lab = "depth",
  y_lab = "sedrate",
  run_random = FALSE,
  rand_simulations = 1000,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  genplot = FALSE,
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  plot_res = 2,
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  method = c("classic", "weighted", "template"),
  tolerance = 0.1,
  whiten = TRUE,
  colour_brewer = NULL
)

Arguments

wavelet

Wavelet object of a depth record (depth in metres), the output of analyse_wavelet (superlet output of class "analyze.superlet" is also accepted). Required (Default=NULL).

sedrate_low

Lowest sedimentation rate to test, in cm/kyr (numeric, > 0). Required (Default=NULL).

sedrate_high

Highest sedimentation rate to test, in cm/kyr (numeric, > sedrate_low). Required (Default=NULL).

spacing

Step between the tested sedimentation rates, in cm/kyr (numeric, > 0); the trial rates are seq(sedrate_low, sedrate_high, by = spacing). Required (Default=NULL).

cycles

Periods of the astronomical cycles in kyr (numeric vector, e.g. c(405, 125, 95, 37, 20)). For each trial sedimentation rate they are converted to periods in metres (cycles * sedrate / 100) and compared with the wavelet spectrum at every depth. Required (Default=c(NULL)).

x_lab

Label of the x-axis (depth) of the plot (character). Default="depth".

y_lab

Label of the y-axis (sedimentation rate) of the plot (character). Default="sedrate".

run_random

Only for method = "classic": also run Monte Carlo simulations in which the spectral peak periods are randomly perturbed, to give the percentile of each fit statistic against this null hypothesis (logical, TRUE or FALSE); without it the percentile elements (5-8) of the output are NA. Default=FALSE.

rand_simulations

Number of random simulations used when run_random = TRUE (integer, > 0; more simulations give more stable percentiles but take longer). Default=1000.

run_multicore

Fit the depth levels in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE); not used by method = "template". Results do not depend on it. Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used when run_multicore = TRUE (integer or NULL). NULL gives an automatic, safe number (physical cores minus one, at most 4, limited by the free memory); change this default with options(waverider.n_cores = ...). A value > 1 also switches on parallel computing. Results do not depend on the number of cores. Default=NULL.

genplot

Plot the result matrix (sedimentation rate against depth) with its depth-averaged profile and a colour key (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

plot_res

Which result matrix is plotted when genplot = TRUE (integer 1-8; only used with method = "classic", the other methods always plot the score): 1 slope coefficient, 2 r squared, 3 number of matched components, 4 difference to the origin, 5 slope coefficient percentile, 6 r squared percentile, 7 number of components percentile, 8 difference to the origin percentile (5-8 need run_random = TRUE). Default=2.

keep_editable

Keep the graphical parameters (par) of the plot after the function returns, so that features can be added to it (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE restores the previous settings. Default=FALSE.

verbose

Show a progress bar over the depth levels (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

method

Method used to compare the cycles with the spectrum (character), one of:

  • "classic": the original peak-based linear-fit method (output identical to earlier versions);

  • "weighted": matches the predicted cycles one-to-one to spectral peaks, weighting by peak power and using a relative (log period) misfit;

  • "template": correlates the spectrum with Gaussian peaks at the predicted periods (no peak picking, fastest and usually most robust).

Default=c("classic", "weighted", "template"), i.e. "classic".

tolerance

Relative period tolerance used by the "weighted" and "template" methods: the standard deviation of the Gaussian misfit in natural-log period (numeric, > 0; 0.1 is about 10 percent). Default=0.1.

whiten

For the "weighted" and "template" methods only: divide the wavelet power of every period by its average over depth before the comparison, which removes the red-noise background (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

Value

Returns a list. For method = "classic" it has the 10 elements below plus score_mat (a heuristic combined score between 0 and 1), best_sedrate (sedimentation rate with the highest score per depth) and method. For the other methods the list has score_mat, best_sedrate, depth, y_axis and method. Use flmw_path to turn score_mat into a smooth sedimentation rate curve with uncertainty.

Elements of the classic result: element 1: slope coefficient element 2: r squared element 3: nr of components element 4: difference to the origin element 5: slope coefficient percentile element 6: r squared percentile element 7: nr of components percentile, element 8: difference to the origin percentile element 9: y-axis values of the matrices which is sedimentation rate element 10: x-axis values of the matrices which is depth

Choosing a method

"classic" keeps the earlier results reproducible. In a synthetic test with strong noise and a sedimentation rate that changes with depth, "weighted" and "template" followed by flmw_path recovered the true curve far better than the classic score (see the NEWS file). "template" needs no peak picking and is the fastest.

Author

Based on the eAsm function of the 'astrochron' R package and the 'eCOCO' and 'COCO' function of the 'Acycle' software

Examples

# \donttest{
#estimate sedimentation rate for the magnetic susceptibility record
# of the Sullivan core of Pas et al., (2018).

mag_wt <- analyse_wavelet(data = mag[1:200, ],
dj = 1/10,
lowerPeriod = 0.1,
upperPeriod = 32,
verbose = FALSE,
omega_nr = 10)

sedrates <- flmw(wavelet = mag_wt,
    sedrate_low = 0.5,
    sedrate_high = 4,
    spacing = 1,
    cycles = c(2376,1600,1180,696,406,110),
    x_lab = "depth",
    y_lab = "sedrate",
    run_random = FALSE,
    rand_simulations = 50, # increase to get better constrainted resutls
    run_multicore = FALSE,
    genplot = FALSE,
    palette_name = "rainbow",
    color_brewer = "grDevices",
    plot_res = 2,
    keep_editable=FALSE,
    verbose=FALSE)

# template method (no peak picking) followed by a smooth sedimentation rate curve
sed_t <- flmw(wavelet = mag_wt, sedrate_low = 0.5, sedrate_high = 4, spacing = 0.5,
    cycles = c(406, 110), method = "template")
sed_path <- flmw_path(sed_t)
# }
